title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the core company handbook topics for Redwood Inference: working culture, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and a short guide to essential internal tools. It is intended as the canonical reference for new hires and managers. For team-specific processes (performance calibration, promotion packet templates, hiring scorecards) see the linked People Ops pages.

1. Working at Redwood — Culture & Expectations

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company that values ownership, pragmatism, and open collaboration. We expect all employees to:
- Prioritize customer reliability and product quality.
- Communicate clearly (async-first, use Confluence + Slack appropriately).
- Document decisions and maintain reproducible runbooks.
- Respect cross-functional partners and keep psychology safe for feedback.

Key behaviors:
- Ship small, iteratively: prefer incremental rollouts and measurable success criteria.
- Data-informed decision-making: use telemetry dashboards and postmortems to learn.
- Mentor and grow others: pair on code reviews, run office hours, and contribute to the internal handbook.

2. Roles & Career Ladders

High-level role families: Engineering, Product, Research/Applied ML, Design, Sales/Go-to-Market, Customer Success, People Ops, Finance & Legal, Security. Each family has a documented ladder with expectations for IC and manager tracks. Below is a concise summary of engineering and product ladders (full ladders live in People Ops -> Career Ladders).

Engineering (IC track) — example levels and core expectations:
- E1 (New grad / Junior): shipping well-scoped tasks, asking for mentorship, learning the codebase.
- E2 (Software Engineer): owning medium-sized components, reliable delivery, writing tests and runbooks.
- E3 (Senior): technical ownership for services, mentoring, system design across subsystems.
- E4 (Staff): cross-team technical leadership, driving architecture decisions, influencing roadmap.
- E5+ (Principal/Distinguished): company-wide technical strategy, critical performance and reliability initiatives.

Engineering (Manager track):
- M1 (First-line manager): people management for a small team, performance management, planning.
- M2 (Manager of Managers): scaling teams, hiring strategy, cross-team alignment.
- M3+ (Director and above): org-level strategy, budget ownership, executive communication.

Product ladder summary:
- PM1: feature-level ownership and execution.
- PM2: product area ownership, stakeholder alignment, metrics ownership.
- PM3+: product strategy, go-to-market coordination, and cross-functional leadership.

Promotion process (summary):
1. Manager initiates promotion conversation during 1:1 or performance cycle.
2. Candidate compiles evidence: impact statements, key projects, feedback, metrics, and a self-assessment.
3. People Ops schedules calibration panel with reviewers from adjacent teams.
4. Panel reviews packet, reaches consensus, and documents rationale on the promotion record.
5. HR updates compensation and communicates next steps.

Timing: promotions typically align with the company performance cycle (biannual) but can be off-cycle for exceptional cases.

3. Benefits & Perks — Summary

Health & Wellness:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer-subsidized premiums.
- Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) options.
- Mental health support: EAP and up to 10 sessions covered for employees and dependents.

Time off & Leave:
- Generous paid time off (flex PTO) with guidance to avoid burnout.
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (role-based top-ups possible).
- Bereavement, jury duty, and short-term disability policies documented in HR portal.

Financial & Retirement:
- Competitive equity package for all full-time hires.
- 401(k) with company match up to stated limits.
- Annual performance bonus eligibility (varies by level/role).

Learning & Development:
- Learning stipend ($1,200/year) and conference budget per team.
- Mentorship programs and regular lunch-and-learns.

Office & Remote Work:
- Hybrid-first policy: teams set local norms; core collaboration days recommended.
- Home office stipend for remote setups and ergonomic equipment allowance.

Perks & Wellbeing:
- Monthly wellness allowance, team social budgets, recognition awards.
- Commuter benefits where applicable.

How to access benefits (steps):
1. Visit the HR portal (People Ops -> Benefits).
2. Complete open enrollment within 30 days of hire or during annual enrollment.
3. Contact benefits@redwood.com for exceptions or special questions.

4. Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Hiring principles:
- Hire for breadth of impact, alignment with company values, and role-specific competency.
- Structured interviews with calibrated rubrics to minimize bias.
- Fast but deliberate: target 3–6 week time-to-offer for most roles.

Interview process (typical for engineering roles):
1. Recruiter screen: role fit, compensation expectations, and relocation/remote logistics.
2. Hiring manager screen: technical depth and team fit.
3. Technical exercise: take-home or paired exercise depending on role.
4. Onsite (or virtual) loop: 4–5 interviews covering system design, coding, and behavioral questions.
5. Debrief & decision: interviewers submit rubrics; hiring committee reviews and extends offer.

Offer & background checks:
- Offers are extended by People Ops in partnership with the hiring manager.
- Employment is contingent on background checks and reference verification per regional requirements.

New hire onboarding (30/60/90 plan):
- Day 0: Welcome email, hardware and tooling access, buddy assignment.
- Week 1: Team onboarding, role expectations, small-first-ship task.
- Month 1 (0–30 days): Complete required trainings (security, code of conduct), shadowing, and first project kickoff.
- Month 2 (30–60 days): Ownership of a defined piece of work, start contributing to team rituals.
- Month 3 (60–90 days): First performance check-in with manager; set development goals and performance milestones.

Manager checklist for new hires (short):
- Prepare 30/60/90 goals and the first PR/review-friendly task.
- Schedule regular 1:1s (weekly for first two months).
- Ensure access to repos, CI, internal docs, and monitoring dashboards.
- Introduce buddy and cross-team stakeholders.

5. Internal Tools Guide — Quick Reference

This section lists the principal internal tools every new employee should know. For detailed how-tos, follow links to each team’s runbooks.

Core systems and primary owners:
- Confluence (company docs) — People Ops / Docs Guild.
- Slack (comms): All engineering and cross-functional channels; use channel naming conventions #team-*, #product-*, #ops-*.
- GitHub (code) — Eng Platform. Follow the repo CONTRIBUTING.md for PR expectations.
- CI/CD (Buildkite) — Eng Infra. Pipelines are documented in eng-infra -> ci-cd-and-build.
- Deployment & infra (Terraform + Argo CD) — Eng Infra / Eng Platform.
- Observability: Grafana dashboards, Loki logs, and Tempo traces — Eng Platform / Eng SRE.
- Secrets & keys (Vault / KMS) — Security & Compliance. Requests go through the secrets-requests workflow.
- HR portal and payroll — People Ops.

Common tasks and commands:
- Clone onboarding repos:
```bash
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/onboarding.git
cd onboarding
./scripts/setup.sh
```
- Requesting access (template):

Subject: Access request — [Your Name] — [Tool]

Body:
1) Business justification
2) Required expiration (if temporary)
3) Manager approval

Send to: access-requests@redwood.com with manager CC.

Access escalation policy:
1. If access is blocked for >24 hours, escalate to the team owner and People Ops.
2. For production emergency access, contact the SRE on-call and open an access ticket with high priority.

6. Manager Resources & Checklists

Hiring checklist for managers:
- Write a clear job spec and add success metrics.
- Create an interview panel with calibrated rubrics.
- Ensure budget approval and People Ops handoff.

Promotion checklist for managers:
- Gather 3–5 concrete examples of impact.
- Collect 360 feedback and peer inputs.
- Draft promotion packet and notify People Ops to schedule calibration.

Offboarding checklist (HR & Manager):
1. Communicate transition plan and knowledge transfer.
2. Revoke access (GitHub, Slack, cloud accounts) on the last working day.
3. Return hardware and complete exit interviews.

7. Policies & Where to Find More

- Security & compliance baseline: See Security & Compliance -> secure-sdlc and audit-logging pages.
- Engineering standards: architecture-and-standards -> infra-standards and api-standards.
- Detailed career ladders and calibration templates: People Ops -> career-ladders.

Appendix A — Example promotion packet template (bulleted)
- Candidate name and role
- Current level and proposed level
- Timeline of projects and impact metrics (quantified where possible)
- Feedback excerpts from peers and managers
- List of growth areas and an agreed development plan

Appendix B — Helpful links
- HR portal: https://hr.redwood.internal/
- Confluence home: https://confluence.redwood.internal/
- Oncall runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks
- Career ladders: /confluence/company-handbook/career-ladders

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (owner_team).
- Review cadence: annual review or sooner when policies change (e.g., benefits or leave).
- How to propose changes: open a PR on the Handbook repo or submit a doc-change request to docs-guild@redwood.com.

End of document.
